questions.q: What does a filtered index restrict?
options: It only covers rows matching a WHERE condition specified in the index definition itself
It only allows one column to be indexed
It restricts which users can query the table
It only works on clustered indexes
questions.explain: This makes the index smaller and faster to scan for queries that match the same filter condition.

questions.q: What does an included column add to a nonclustered index?
options: Extra column data stored directly in the index, without making it part of the search key
A new WHERE clause restricting the index
An additional clustered index on the same table
A foreign key constraint
questions.explain: INCLUDE (ListPrice) stores that column's data in the index without indexing/sorting on it.

options: An index that contains every column a specific query needs, avoiding a lookup back to the full row
An index that covers every table in the database
A synonym for a clustered index
An index that automatically updates itself nightly
questions.explain: If a query selects only columns present in the index (search key + included columns), the index alone satisfies it.

questions.q: What is the tradeoff for using filtered indexes and included columns?
options: Some extra storage cost in exchange for avoiding repeated, larger runtime costs on a frequently-run query pattern
They always make queries slower but save storage
They eliminate the need for a clustered index entirely
There is no tradeoff — they are strictly free performance gains
questions.explain: A filtered index needs metadata; an included column duplicates data — both are usually worth it for frequent queries.

questions.q: Can a single index be both filtered and include extra columns at the same time?
options: Yes — a narrow, covering index for exactly one common query pattern
No, an index must choose one technique or the other
Only clustered indexes can combine both features
Only if the table has no primary key
questions.explain: The combined example shows a nonclustered index with both INCLUDE and WHERE applied together.
